docs.title: ETLRelay
docs.text:
ETLRelay is a lightweight Python framework for composing batch-oriented extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines.

Its core execution model is:

Source → Processor(s) → Sink

A source produces batches, processors transform them, and a sink consumes the processed output. For file workflows, storage access is independent of format-specific reading and writing.

docs.title: Current release: 0.6.0
docs.text:
ETLRelay 0.6.0 adds declarative, versioned YAML configuration while preserving direct Python composition. The YAML configuration path loads and validates a mapping-shaped document, resolves explicit built-in component registrations, preflights required SQL connection-variable references, and then builds a runtime pipeline.

Capabilities include:

  • Arrow-backed Batch data and synchronous pipeline execution.
  • Local filesystem access with path-containment validation.
  • CSV and Parquet file input/output.
  • Built-in column selection, column renaming, and row filtering processors.
  • SQLAlchemy-backed SqlSource and append-only SqlSink.
  • YAML schema version 1, strict configuration validation, and path-qualified validation errors.
  • A shared default component catalog and PipelineBuilder for configuration-built pipelines.
  • Integration and functional coverage for file, SQLite, and mixed source/sink combinations.

SQLite is the reference SQL integration-test backend. Other SQLAlchemy dialects require their appropriate drivers and application-level verification. SQL sink tables must already exist and accept the output columns. ETLRelay remains pre-1.0 software; public APIs may evolve between minor versions.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The v0.6.0 YAML format supports local CSV/Parquet files and SQL sources/sinks, with select_columns, rename_columns, and filter_rows processors. Schema version 1 has a fixed built-in component set. It is not a general dynamic plugin system. A command-line interface remains planned for a later milestone.

Create the default component catalog and its shared dependencies.

The catalog registers CSV and Parquet readers and writers, local filesystem storage, file and SQL sources and sinks, and the select_columns, rename_columns, and filter_rows processors. It also assembles the dispatchers and root configuration validator.

A single set of registries is shared between the corresponding validators and factories, and the same SQL engine factory is supplied to both SQL component factories.

The tabular file-format registry is separate from key-value document readers such as YamlReader, which are not registered as tabular data formats.

docs.title: etlrelay.config.pipeline_builder.PipelineBuilder
docs.text:
Build runtime pipelines from validated configuration mappings.

The builder resolves source, processor, and sink registrations before invoking component factories. SQL environment references are preflighted before component construction to prevent missing or empty environment variables from causing partial pipeline construction.

getenv provides a lightweight environment lookup for isolated builder use and tests. In the default application composition, the shared SqlEngineFactory should be supplied so successful preflight makes resolved connection URLs available to SQL component factories.

The builder does not execute the pipeline it constructs. When a shared SQL engine factory is supplied, the caller is responsible for closing the builder after pipeline execution to release the factory's resources.

docs.text:
Resolve SQL connection URLs and manage SQLAlchemy engine lifecycles.

Environment-variable references must pass preflight before engines can be created. Successful preflight stores resolved connection URLs without creating engines. Engines are created on demand and cached by environment variable name.

The factory owns the engines it creates and disposes of them when close() is called. Closing also discards resolved connection URLs. Environment lookup and engine creation can be injected for testing.

docs.title: preflight(references)
docs.text:
Resolve and validate all referenced connection environment variables.

The mapping associates configuration paths with environment-variable names. Each unique variable is read once, and missing or empty values are aggregated into a single error. No engines are created during preflight.

A successful preflight replaces any previous resolved URL set. A failed preflight leaves resolved URLs unavailable for engine creation. Preflight cannot be repeated while the factory has active engines.

Note

docs.title: close()

Engine disposal is attempted in reverse creation order. The factory clears its engine cache and resolved URLs before disposal, and continues disposing remaining engines if one fails. Calling this method more than once is safe.

docs.title: etlrelay.pipeline.pipeline.Pipeline
docs.text:
Coordinate batch processing between a source, processors, and a sink.

The pipeline obtains batches from a source, applies each configured processor in sequence, validates the resulting output schemas, and passes compatible batches to the sink.

The first processed output batch establishes the expected schema for the run. Subsequent output batches must have matching field names, field order, Arrow types, and nullability. Schema metadata differences are ignored. Zero-row batches participate in schema validation.

Processing is lazy and does not buffer all batches before writing. If a later batch has an incompatible schema, a ValueError is raised before that batch is yielded to the sink. Batches successfully written before a later failure are not rolled back.

Exceptions from the source, processors, or sink otherwise propagate to the caller.

Filter a batch using a single column comparison predicate.

Supported operators are ==, !=, <, <=, >, and >=. Comparisons use Apache Arrow compute operations without custom casting.

Rows whose comparison evaluates to false or null are excluded. The input schema is preserved, including when no rows match.

The processor can be reused across batches without retaining batch-specific state.

Example

from etlrelay.processors import FilterRows

processor = FilterRows(column="age", operator=">=", value=18) result = processor.process(batch)

Type Description ValueError

If the comparison operator is unsupported.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
ETLRelay composes batch-oriented ETL pipelines from a source, an ordered sequence of processors, and a sink.

Source → Processor(s) → Sink

A source produces batches, processors transform them, and a sink consumes the processed output. For file workflows, ETLRelay separates storage access from format-specific reading and writing.

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
A Batch wraps a pyarrow.Table and provides the common tabular data representation used throughout ETLRelay.

The table retains its values and Arrow schema, including field names, field order, data types, and nullability. A processor may change the schema as part of a transformation; otherwise, the schema is preserved.

A batch containing zero rows is still a valid batch. Its schema remains available even when it contains no data rows.

docs.title: Source, Processor, and Sink
docs.text:
A Source implements read() and produces an iterable of batches.

A Processor implements:

process(batch: Batch) -> Batch

Processors operate on individual batches. The pipeline applies them in their configured order, passing each processor's output to the next processor. ETLRelay includes processors for selecting columns, renaming columns, and filtering rows. Applications can also provide implementations that satisfy the processor contract.

A Sink consumes an iterable of processed batches. A file sink composes a storage implementation with a writer to write batches to a configured destination.

docs.title: Storage and File Formats
docs.text:
Storage provides binary streams; readers and writers handle file formats.

FileSource → FileSystem → BinaryIO → Reader → Batch

Batch iterable → Writer → BinaryIO → FileSystem → Destination

FileSource composes a filesystem with a reader. FileSink composes a filesystem with a writer. This separates resource access from format-specific parsing and serialization.

The built-in local storage and tabular formats are LocalFileSystem, CSV, and Parquet. Select the reader and writer explicitly when composing FileSource and FileSink; the file extension does not select a format automatically.

docs.title: CSV and Parquet Behavior
docs.text:
Behavior CSV Parquet Representation Text; no embedded Arrow schema Columnar binary format with schema and type information Reading types PyArrow infers types from text; exact schema round trips are not guaranteed Preserves supported schema/type information represented in the file Multiple batches Serializes batches in order; a CSV stream has one header written by the first batch Serializes batches in order into one Parquet file Zero-row batch with schema Can write a header-only CSV Writes a valid schema-bearing zero-row Parquet file; the reader yields an empty batch with the schema Empty batch iterable Writes no bytes Raises WriterError because no schema is available to initialize the file Stream requirements Binary stream Reader requires a seekable binary stream; writer requires a writable binary stream supported by PyArrow

A zero-row batch and an empty batch iterable are different: the former still carries an Arrow schema; the latter carries no batch from which a schema can be obtained. ParquetWriter uses the first batch's schema and requires following batches to have the same schema. ETLRelay does not merge incompatible schemas or automatically cast batches.

The component that opens a stream retains responsibility for its lifecycle; readers and writers must not close caller-owned streams.

docs.title: Declarative Configuration
docs.text:
ETLRelay 0.6.0 adds schema-versioned YAML configuration as an alternative to direct Python composition. The supported configuration surface is deliberately fixed: file and SQL sources/sinks, local storage, CSV/Parquet file formats, and the built-in column-selection, renaming, and row-filtering processors.

The workflow is:

YAML file
   ↓
ConfigLoader + KeyValueReader/YamlReader
   ↓
ConfigValidator
   ↓
Validated mapping
   ↓
PipelineBuilder + shared ComponentCatalog
   ↓
Pipeline
   ↓
Pipeline.run()

A mapping-shaped configuration document is not a tabular Batch stream. KeyValueReader is a separate protocol from the current tabular Reader protocol. YamlReader handles YAML syntax and document shape; ConfigValidator handles ETLRelay's schema; PipelineBuilder resolves explicit registrations and constructs runtime components. Neither loading nor schema validation builds or executes a pipeline.

Configuration schema version 1 requires exactly version, source, processors, and sink. Unknown fields and unsupported component types are rejected. SQL source/sink connection URLs are referenced by environment-variable name, then checked during builder preflight before component factories and source/sink I/O begin. See YAML Configuration for properties, combinations, errors, and examples.

docs.title: Pipeline Execution
docs.text:
Pipeline coordinates the source, processors, and sink. Execution is synchronous, and batches are processed sequentially in source order.

The pipeline does not buffer all source batches before writing. Processed batches are yielded incrementally to the sink.

docs.title: Output Schema Compatibility
docs.text:
The first processed output batch establishes the expected schema for a pipeline run. Every subsequent processed output batch must have a compatible schema.

Compatibility requires matching:

  • Field names
  • Field order
  • Arrow field types
  • Field nullability

Schema metadata differences are ignored when checking compatibility. Schema validation takes place after all configured processors have run. This allows processors to normalize inputs with different schemas into compatible output schemas.

If a processed batch has an incompatible schema, the pipeline raises ValueError before yielding that batch to the sink. The pipeline does not automatically merge schemas, cast values, or reconcile incompatible outputs. Zero-row batches participate in schema validation just like non-empty batches.

docs.title: Empty Sources and Zero-Row Batches
docs.text:
An empty source iterable and a zero-row batch represent different conditions.

  • Zero-row batch: The source produces a Batch containing a zero-row Arrow table. The batch passes through the configured processors, participates in schema validation, and is delivered to the sink if processing succeeds.
  • Empty source iterable: The source produces no batches. No processors are called, and the sink is not invoked.

The presence of a batch, rather than its row count, determines whether the pipeline has data to process.

docs.title: Exceptions and Partial Writes
docs.text:
Exceptions raised while reading from a source, iterating over its batches, processing a batch, validating its output schema, or writing to a sink propagate to the caller. ETLRelay does not wrap these errors in a separate pipeline exception hierarchy.

If a later batch fails, batches successfully written before the failure are not automatically rolled back. The pipeline does not provide transactional execution across multiple batches.

docs.title: Current Scope
docs.text:
ETLRelay provides synchronous, batch-oriented execution with local CSV/Parquet I/O, SQLAlchemy-backed SQL sources/sinks, a small set of built-in processors, and YAML-driven construction. SQLite is the reference SQL integration-test backend; other SQLAlchemy dialects require appropriate drivers and independent verification. SQL sink tables must already exist and be compatible with the output columns.

S3, HDFS, and other remote-storage backends remain outside the planned v1.0.0 scope. Scheduling, distributed execution, parallel processing, automatic retries, generic plugins, and automatic schema reconciliation are not provided by the current implementation. Additional capabilities should be introduced only when concrete requirements justify them.

docs.title: YAML Configuration
docs.text:
ETLRelay 0.6.0 supports declarative pipeline configuration using a versioned YAML document. Configuration schema version 1 exposes the built-in components only; it is not a general-purpose plugin system and does not permit arbitrary Python construction.

Use this page as the canonical reference for the schema. Getting Started demonstrates how to load, build, and execute a configuration; the configuration architecture pages explain the internal boundaries.

docs.title: Configuration lifecycle
docs.text:
Configuration loading, validation, construction, and execution are separate stages:

  1. ConfigLoader opens and parses the configuration document through FileSystem and KeyValueReader (YamlReader is the built-in implementation).
  2. ConfigValidator checks schema version 1 and delegates to the source, ordered processor-sequence, and sink validators. It raises ConfigurationError for schema failures.
  3. PipelineBuilder resolves the source, sink, and processor registrations, then preflights SQL environment-variable references.
  4. Only after component types and SQL references pass preflight does the builder invoke component factories and return a Pipeline.
  5. The caller runs the pipeline with pipeline.run() and closes the builder after execution to release SQL engines owned by the shared factory.

The configuration file itself must be opened to read it. Invalid schema and missing/empty SQL connection variables are rejected before source/sink data operations begin. This is not a guarantee against runtime file, query, database, schema, processor, or sink failures.

docs.title: Root schema
docs.text:
Every schema-v1 document must contain exactly these top-level properties:

Property Required Type Contract version Yes integer Must be the integer 1; YAML Boolean true is not accepted as version 1. source Yes mapping One supported source definition. processors Yes list Ordered processor definitions. An empty list is valid and passes batches through unchanged. sink Yes mapping One supported sink definition.

Unknown top-level properties are rejected. Component definitions also have closed property sets, so misspelled or unsupported fields are rejected rather than ignored. Duplicate YAML mapping keys are rejected, including duplicates after YAML merge-key flattening.

The schema version is independent of the ETLRelay package version. Version 1 has no implicit fallback or migration. Incompatible configuration-structure changes require a new schema version; existing version-1 property meanings must remain stable.

docs.title: Supported component/property matrix
docs.text:
Area type / name Properties beyond type Notes Source file path, format, storage Format must support reading. Source sql connection_url_env, query; optional parameters Uses a preflighted connection URL from the named environment variable. Sink file path, format, storage Format must support writing. Sink sql connection_url_env, table_name; optional schema Appends to an existing table. Processor select_columns columns Ordered list of unique string column names. Processor rename_columns mapping Mapping of string source names to string target names. Processor filter_rows column, operator, value Predicate value must be a string, integer, float, or Boolean. Storage local Optional base_path Defaults to .. File input format csv, parquet source.format Each registered format must support reading. File output format csv, parquet sink.format Each registered format must support writing.

No other source, sink, processor, storage backend, or file format is supported by schema version 1.

docs.title: File source and sink
docs.text:
A file source and file sink use the same required property names:

Property Required Type Meaning type Yes string: file Selects the file source or sink. path Yes non-empty string Input or output path. format Yes string: csv or parquet Explicitly selects a registered reader or writer. Format is not inferred from the filename extension. storage Yes mapping Storage component configuration. storage.type Yes string: local Selects LocalFileSystem. storage.base_path No non-empty string Permitted base directory; defaults to ..

Relative base_path values are resolved from the process working directory; relative path values are resolved under that base directory. Absolute paths are accepted only if they remain within the configured base. PathValidator enforces path containment; it is not a complete OS-level sandbox.

The base directory and any needed parent directories must already exist. Local output creates a new file if necessary and truncates an existing output file; it does not create missing parent directories.

Source and sink formats are selected independently, so all four file-to-file combinations are supported: CSV→CSV, CSV→Parquet, Parquet→CSV, and Parquet→Parquet.

docs.title: SQL source
docs.text:
Property Required Type Meaning type Yes string: sql Selects SqlSource. connection_url_env Yes non-empty string Name of an environment variable containing the SQLAlchemy connection URL. query Yes non-empty string Caller-authored SQL query. Use named bind parameters for query values. parameters No mapping Named bind-parameter values. Keys must be strings; values may be strings, integers, floats, Booleans, or null.

Nested mappings and sequences are not supported as query-parameter values. Bound parameters are for values, not identifiers such as table or column names. Configuration validation does not parse SQL or enforce database authorization policy.

Example:

source:
  type: sql
  connection_url_env: ETLRELAY_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL
  query: "SELECT id, amount, state FROM source_records WHERE state = :state ORDER BY id"
  parameters:
    state: ready

docs.title: SQL sink
docs.text:
Property Required Type Meaning type Yes string: sql Selects SqlSink. connection_url_env Yes non-empty string Name of an environment variable containing the SQLAlchemy connection URL. table_name Yes non-empty string Existing destination table to append rows to. schema No non-empty string Optional database schema name.

The destination table must already exist and accept the processed batch columns. The sink does not create, truncate, replace, or migrate tables. Each non-empty batch is written in its own transaction; a later failure does not roll back earlier committed batches. SQLite is the reference integration-test backend. Other SQLAlchemy dialects require their relevant drivers and independent verification.

SQL source and sink components can use the same environment-variable name or different names.

docs.title: Processor definitions
docs.text: The processors property is an ordered list. Processor n receives the output of processor n-1. An empty list is valid; omitting the property is invalid.

docs.title: select_columns
docs.text:
Property Required Type Contract type Yes string: select_columns Processor discriminator. columns Yes list of strings Names must be unique. The list determines output column order.

Column existence depends on the data schema and can fail during execution.

docs.title: rename_columns
docs.text:
Property Required Type Contract type Yes string: rename_columns Processor discriminator. mapping Yes mapping of string to string Source column name to desired column name.

The validator checks that the mapping and its keys/values have the required types. Whether source columns exist and whether final column names conflict is checked against the batch schema during processing.

docs.title: filter_rows
docs.text:
Property Required Type Contract type Yes string: filter_rows Processor discriminator. column Yes non-empty string Column to compare. operator Yes string One of ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=. value Yes string, integer, float, or Boolean null, mappings, and sequences are not accepted.

Column existence and comparison compatibility depend on the input data and may therefore fail at execution time. The validator does not inspect file contents or execute the processor.

docs.title: Supported source/sink combinations
docs.text:
The configured source and sink are independently selected from the supported formats and component types. This produces nine format/component combinations:

Source Sink Status and constraints CSV file CSV file Supported. CSV file Parquet file Supported. Parquet file CSV file Supported. Parquet file Parquet file Supported. CSV file SQL Supported. SQL target table must exist and accept the output columns. Parquet file SQL Supported. SQL target table must exist and accept the output columns. SQL CSV file Supported. Output path/base directory must be permitted and available. SQL Parquet file Supported. Output path/base directory must be permitted and available. SQL SQL Supported. Target table must exist and accept the output columns; source and sink may use same or separate connection variables.

These are supported combinations, not a guarantee that arbitrary queries, schemas, paths, values, or destination tables will work. Runtime checks and external system errors still apply.

docs.title: Complete runnable examples
docs.text:
The repository's examples/configuration/ directory contains nine schema-v1 YAML files for the combinations above, a reusable runner, a data-preparation script, and input setup for local CSV, Parquet, and SQLite. See Getting Started for setup and run commands. The examples use a small schema with id, amount, and state columns; the pipeline selects id and amount, filters amount >= 0, and renames id to record_id.

  • Example runner
  • Prepare example data
  • Configuration examples directory

The examples expect commands to be run from the repository root so relative paths are interpreted consistently. The SQL examples require the environment variables shown below to point at the SQLite demo databases created by prepare_demo_data.py:

export ETLRELAY_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///examples/configuration/data/source.db"
export ETLRELAY_SINK_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///examples/configuration/data/sink.db"

Only examples that use SQL need the corresponding variable. The values above are non-secret local SQLite URLs; real connection URLs may contain credentials and must not be placed directly in YAML.

docs.title: Environment variables and secrets
docs.text:
The configuration stores the environment-variable name, not the resolved URL. For example, connection_url_env: ETLRELAY_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL tells the builder which environment variable to resolve.

  • Set required variables in the process environment before building a SQL pipeline.
  • Missing and empty variable values cause preflight to fail before ETL component factories are invoked or source/sink I/O begins.
  • Each unique referenced variable is resolved once during preflight.
  • Error messages identify the configuration path and variable name, but must not include the resolved URL or credentials.
  • Never put passwords, tokens, or credential-bearing connection URLs directly in YAML examples or commit them to version control.

Environment variables provide secret indirection, not a dedicated secrets vault. Deployment-specific secret injection, access control, rotation, and environment hygiene remain the application's responsibility. See Security.

docs.title: Validation and representative errors
docs.text:
Validation rejects malformed documents and unsupported configuration before runtime construction. Examples of actionable error messages include:

Problem Example message Unsupported schema version version must be the integer 1. Missing root field Required top-level field 'processors' is missing. Unsupported property sink.destination is not a supported field. Unsupported format source.format 'xlsx' is not supported for reading. Invalid filter operator processors[0].operator must be one of '==', '!=', '<', '<=', '>', '>='. Missing SQL environment variable source.connection_url_env references missing or empty environment variable 'ETLRELAY_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL'.

The full SQL preflight error is wrapped in PipelineBuildError; it may aggregate multiple missing references into one message. Component validators normally return lists of path-qualified errors; the root ConfigValidator raises ConfigurationError containing those validation errors.

YAML syntax/document errors are distinct from schema errors. YamlReader rejects malformed YAML, duplicate mapping keys, multiple documents, a non-mapping root, and non-string root keys. ConfigLoader does not translate filesystem or reader exceptions into ConfigurationError by default.

Validation does not guarantee that source files exist, SQL parses or executes, destination tables exist, columns match the data, or output operations will succeed. Those conditions depend on runtime components and external resources.

docs.title: Schema security and scope
docs.text:
• YAML is parsed with a safe loader; arbitrary Python object construction is not part of configuration loading.
  • Component types resolve only through explicit built-in registries. Schema v1 does not provide dynamic imports, user code evaluation, or arbitrary plugin loading.
  • SQL text remains caller-authored SQL. Bind values rather than interpolating untrusted values, and validate/allowlist dynamic identifiers separately.
  • Local path validation is a containment check, not a full OS sandbox or authorization policy.
  • JSON configuration, remote storage, additional formats, additional processors, a general plugin system, a CLI, schema migrations, and SQL table-creation modes are not part of the v0.6.0 YAML contract.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: ETLRelay uses Python 3.12+, Nix flakes for a reproducible development environment, uv for Python dependencies and lockfiles, pytest for tests, Ruff for linting and formatting, Pyright for static typing, MkDocs for documentation, GitHub Actions for CI, and PyPI for distribution.

docs.title: Install the development environment
docs.text:
From the repository root, synchronize the committed lockfile and all dependency groups:

uv sync --locked --all-groups

Run checks in the project's supported Nix development environment when tools such as Ruff or Pyright are supplied by Nix rather than the Python environment. Do not change runtime dependencies solely to make a development tool available.

docs.title: Run quality checks
docs.text:
Run the repository's configured tests and quality checks:

uv run pytest --cov=etlrelay --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=90.1
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run pyright
uv run mkdocs build --strict

The configured coverage gate requires at least 90.1% reported coverage. If a known static-analysis command fails because of an existing environment or baseline issue, record its exact diagnostic and compare it with the established baseline rather than silently treating it as a pass.

For a release candidate, also build and validate the distributions:

uv build
uvx --from 'twine>=7,<8' twine check dist/*

Follow docs/development/release-automation.md and RELEASE_CHECKS.md for the complete release process and result-recording requirements.

docs.title: Preview documentation
docs.text:
Start the local documentation server from the repository root:

uv run mkdocs serve

MkDocs serves a preview and rebuilds pages when documentation files change. Review changed pages in the rendered site, including Mermaid diagrams and navigation links.

docs.title: Validate documentation
docs.text:
Build the documentation with warnings treated as errors:

uv run mkdocs build --strict

The build output is written to site/. Do not commit generated site/ files; ensure site/ is listed in .gitignore.

The API reference uses mkdocstrings to render the documented modules from src/. When a module path or public API changes, update docs/api-reference.md and any affected user-facing or architecture pages, then ensure the strict build passes.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: ETLRelay 0.6.0 supports both direct Python composition and versioned YAML configuration. This guide starts with YAML—the new declarative interface—and then explains where to go for the direct component API.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer.
  • ETLRelay 0.6.0.
  • A local filesystem directory where the example data and outputs can be stored.

For the full runnable examples, clone the repository and install the package in an environment using the repository's supported Python setup:

git clone https://github.com/apaquette/ETLRelay.git
cd ETLRelay
python -m pip install -e .

The examples are kept under examples/configuration/ so that their YAML files, preparation script, and runner can be used together. If you are using the published package rather than a checkout, use the package version and Python environment appropriate to your installation, and obtain the examples from the v0.6.0 repository tag.

docs.title: Prepare the demonstration data
docs.text:
Run the preparation script from the repository root:

python examples/configuration/prepare_demo_data.py

It creates a small CSV input file, a corresponding Parquet input file, and source/target SQLite databases in examples/configuration/data/. The target table is deliberately created before the SQL sink runs because SqlSink appends to an existing table; it does not create or migrate tables.

The sample input contains id, amount, and state. The YAML processors select id and amount, keep rows where amount >= 0, and rename id to record_id.

docs.title: Run a YAML pipeline
docs.text:
The runner loads the YAML document through ConfigLoader, validates it using the default component catalog, constructs the pipeline with PipelineBuilder, executes it, and closes the shared SQL engine factory in a finally block.

Run a CSV-to-CSV pipeline:

python examples/configuration/run.py examples/configuration/csv_to_csv.yaml

Run a CSV-to-Parquet pipeline:

python examples/configuration/run.py examples/configuration/csv_to_parquet.yaml

The runner accepts any of the nine YAML examples in examples/configuration/: four file-to-file format pairs, two file-to-SQL pairs, two SQL-to-file pairs, and one SQL-to-SQL pair. Outputs are written beneath examples/configuration/data/.

For SQL examples, configure the demo database URLs in the process environment:

export ETLRELAY_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///examples/configuration/data/source.db"
export ETLRELAY_SINK_DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///examples/configuration/data/sink.db"

Then run, for example:

python examples/configuration/run.py examples/configuration/sql_to_sql.yaml

Each SQL configuration references the variable name in its connection_url_env field. The YAML file never contains the resolved URL. These demo URLs are local and contain no credentials; do not put credential-bearing connection URLs or passwords into configuration files.

docs.title: Understand the YAML pipeline
docs.text:
A typical file pipeline has four required top-level properties: version, source, processors, and sink.

version: 1

source:
  type: file
  path: examples/configuration/data/input.csv
  format: csv
  storage:
    type: local
    base_path: .

processors:
  - type: select_columns
    columns: [id, amount]
  - type: filter_rows
    column: amount
    operator: ">="
    value: 0
  - type: rename_columns
    mapping:
      id: record_id

sink:
  type: file
  path: examples/configuration/data/output.csv
  format: csv
  storage:
    type: local
    base_path: .

The version property is the configuration schema version, currently integer 1; it is independent of the Python package version 0.6.0. A processors list is required, but processors: [] is valid and passes batches through without transformations.

Processor order matters: select_columns drops state, filter_rows removes negative amounts, and rename_columns changes the retained id field to record_id. Formats are explicit; ETLRelay does not infer them from file extensions.

docs.title: Validation and errors
docs.text:
The loader's validation stage checks the configuration structure, required fields, schema version, component names, and property types. Invalid configuration is rejected before source/sink operations and pipeline execution.

For example:

  • An unknown property such as sink.destination is rejected.
  • An unsupported file format is rejected using the format registry's reading/writing capability.
  • A filter operator outside ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= is rejected.
  • A missing or empty SQL connection environment variable fails during build-time preflight, before ETL component factories are invoked.

Schema validation does not prove that the named input file exists, that a selected column is present in the runtime schema, that SQL will succeed, or that the destination table is compatible. These are runtime conditions. See YAML Configuration for the full schema and Configuration Validation Architecture for validation boundaries.

docs.title: Programmatic composition remains supported
docs.text:
The YAML interface is additive; direct Python construction remains available. This is still supported:

from pathlib import Path

from etlrelay.pipeline import Pipeline
from etlrelay.processors import FilterRows, RenameColumns, SelectColumns
from etlrelay.readers import CsvReader
from etlrelay.security import PathValidator
from etlrelay.sinks import FileSink
from etlrelay.sources import FileSource
from etlrelay.storage import LocalFileSystem
from etlrelay.writers import CsvWriter

base = Path("data").resolve()
storage = LocalFileSystem(path_validator=PathValidator(base_path=base))
pipeline = Pipeline(
    source=FileSource(path="input.csv", storage=storage, reader=CsvReader()),
    processors=[
        SelectColumns(columns=["name", "age"]),
        RenameColumns(mapping={"name": "customer_name"}),
        FilterRows(column="age", operator=">=", value=18),
    ],
    sink=FileSink(path="output.csv", storage=storage, writer=CsvWriter()),
)
pipeline.run()

For this direct API example, data/input.csv must exist and the output is data/output.csv. Engine lifecycle for direct SqlSource/SqlSink components remains caller-owned; the managed engine lifecycle described above applies to configuration-built pipelines using the shared SqlEngineFactory.

docs.title: More details
docs.text:
• YAML Configuration — versioned schema, component matrix, secret handling, and errors.
  • Core Concepts — batches, schema behavior, empty inputs, and synchronous execution.
  • API Reference — public interfaces and classes.
  • Configuration Loading Architecture — reader/loader boundaries.
  • Component Registry Architecture — registries, factories, and default catalog.
  • Security — path containment and SQL credential handling.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This roadmap defines incremental, testable milestones from the current YAML-configurable, batch-oriented ETL implementation to a stable ETLRelay 1.0.0 release.

The target for 1.0.0 is a lightweight, synchronous, batch-oriented ETL framework that can read from local files or SQL, apply a small set of transformations, and write to local files or SQL. File storage and serialization remain separate concerns. YAML configuration and a small CLI make pipelines usable without writing Python for every job.

The roadmap is feature-led, not date-led. A version should be released when its acceptance criteria are met; the version numbers are proposed milestones, not a promise to publish every milestone on a fixed schedule.

docs.title: Current project status
docs.text:
Status Version Milestone Released 0.1.0 Experimental local CSV pipeline Released 0.1.x Stabilization and compatible fixes Released 0.2.0 Batch contract and built-in processors Released 0.3.0 Parquet format support Released 0.4.0 Storage contract stabilization Released 0.5.0 SQL source and sink Released 0.6.0 YAML configuration and runtime pipeline construction Planned 0.7.0 onward CLI and v1.0 readiness milestones

The latest released milestone is 0.6.0. Releases 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 stabilized local filesystem behavior and added SQL source/sink support; 0.6.0 adds versioned YAML loading and validation, explicit component registrations, a shared default component catalog, SQL environment preflight, and configuration-driven pipeline construction. The CLI remains planned for 0.7.0. Later milestones describe intended scope and may be revised as implementation and testing clarify dependencies.

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text:
ETLRelay is in initial development, so 0.y.z is appropriate while the public API is still evolving. Semantic Versioning explicitly says that a 0.y.z public API should not yet be considered stable and recommends 0.1.0 as a reasonable starting point. See Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 and the Python Packaging User Guide's versioning discussion.

Until 1.0.0:

  • Use a patch release such as 0.1.1 for compatible fixes to a published release.
  • Use a minor release such as 0.2.0 for a coherent feature milestone. Public APIs may still evolve before 1.0.0, but document notable breaking changes.
  • Never replace or modify an already-published release. Publish a new version instead.
  • Use a release candidate such as 1.0.0rc1 only when the intended 1.0.0 feature set is complete and the remaining work is validation and defect correction.

docs.title: 0.1.0 — Experimental local CSV pipeline (released)
docs.text:
Outcome: Published the initial experimental local CSV pipeline. This release established the initial file-to-file execution path; it did not promise API stability.

The original release scope covered:

  • Batch backed by an Apache Arrow table.
  • Source, Processor, and Sink protocols.
  • Synchronous Pipeline orchestration.
  • PathValidator for local path containment.
  • FileSystem protocol and LocalFileSystem implementation.
  • Stream-based Reader and Writer protocols.
  • CsvReader and CsvWriter.
  • FileSource and FileSink composed from storage and format components.
  • Unit, integration, and functional tests for the local CSV path.
  • Architecture and usage documentation that matches the actual implementation.

The original release checks are preserved below as historical reference, not as open tasks for the current milestone.

Original release checks:

  • Full test suite, Ruff lint/format, and configured Pyright checks.
  • Successful source distribution and wheel builds.
  • Clean-environment installation and import/usage smoke test.
  • Accurate README instructions and example.
  • Correct project metadata, licence, package contents, and supported Python version.
  • Release notes describing pre-1.0.0 API evolution.
  • Git tag and retained release artifacts.

For future releases, uv build is the recommended package-build check. The Python Packaging User Guide describes building source and wheel distributions and supports using TestPyPI to rehearse publication: Building and Publishing.

docs.title: 0.1.x — Stabilize the first release (released patch line)
docs.text:
Goal: Correct defects found during initial use without expanding the feature set unnecessarily.

Scope:

  • Fix defects in the pipeline, batch, path validation, local storage, CSV reading, or CSV writing.
  • Improve error messages where they currently obscure the failing operation.
  • Correct packaging, installation, documentation, and typing issues.

Do not use patch releases to sneak in unrelated, large features.

docs.title: 0.2.0 — Batch contract and built-in processors (released)
docs.text:
Goal: Make ETLRelay useful for more than an untransformed file copy.

Scope:

  • Document and test Batch semantics, including schemas, types, zero-row tables, and empty iterables.
  • Define what happens when batches in one output stream have incompatible schemas.
  • Add a small set of processors, prioritizing:
  • SelectColumns;
  • RenameColumns;
  • FilterRows with a deliberately limited and documented predicate model.
  • Verify processor ordering and behavior across multiple batches.
  • Keep the processor interface as process(batch) -> Batch.

Done when: A tested local CSV pipeline can select, rename, and filter columns/rows while preserving documented schema and empty-batch behavior.

Not in scope: A general-purpose expression language, user-supplied code evaluation, or a large processor catalogue.

docs.title: 0.3.0 — Parquet format support (released)
docs.text:
Goal: Support a second high-value tabular format while retaining the format/storage boundary.

Scope:

  • Implement ParquetReader and ParquetWriter against the existing stream-based reader/writer protocols where the chosen Arrow APIs support that contract.
  • Test schema and type preservation, empty data, malformed input, and round trips.
  • Verify that the same reader/writer components work with LocalFileSystem without special cases in FileSource or FileSink.
  • Document CSV and Parquet behavior, including limitations and format-specific differences.

Done when: Local CSV and Parquet sources/sinks work through the same file composition model.

docs.title: 0.4.0 — Storage contract stabilization (released)
docs.text:
Outcome: Stabilized and documented the FileSystem/LocalFileSystem contract used by the local-file pipelines. The release specifies stream ownership and cleanup, read/write behavior, missing-path handling, path containment, overwrite behavior, and error propagation.

The release retained local filesystem support only. S3, HDFS, and other remote-storage backends remain outside both the v0.4.0 milestone and the planned v1.0.0 scope. Additional storage/platform integrations may be reviewed after v1.0.0 if concrete requirements justify them; none is promised by this roadmap.

Done when: The contract is explicit and tested, LocalFileSystem satisfies it, and existing CSV/Parquet pipelines remain functional.

docs.title: 0.5.0 — SQL source and sink (released)
docs.text:
Outcome: Added SQLAlchemy-backed SqlSource and SqlSink as direct implementations of the core source/sink contracts, independent of file storage and reader/writer abstractions.

The release supports bound query-value parameters, conversion of query results to Arrow-backed batches, and append-only insertion into existing destination tables. SQLite provides repeatable integration coverage for reads, writes, SQL round trips, and mixed file/SQL functional pipelines.

The caller owns the SQLAlchemy engine. SqlSource closes query results/connections after reading; SqlSink opens one transaction per non-empty batch. Consequently, earlier batches remain committed if a later batch fails. An empty SQL query returns no batches. The sink skips zero-row batches and requires the destination table to exist with compatible columns.

The SQL API does not implement replace, ORM-model integration, table creation/schema migrations, automatic retries, or pipeline-wide transactions. SQLite is the reference integration backend; support for other SQLAlchemy dialects requires the relevant driver and verification.

Done when: SQL input and append-only output compose with ETLRelay pipelines, value parameters are bound, and the behavior and limitations are documented and tested.

docs.title: 0.6.0 — Declarative YAML configuration (released)
docs.text:
Outcome: Added versioned YAML configuration and construction of runtime pipelines from validated mappings while preserving the direct Python APIs.

The release includes:

  • KeyValueReader and YamlReader for safe, mapping-shaped YAML documents, including duplicate-key rejection and root mapping/string-key checks.
  • ConfigLoader to coordinate configuration file access, parsing, and schema validation.
  • ConfigValidator, ConfigurationError, component-specific validators, and family dispatchers for source, sink, storage, and processor configuration.
  • ComponentRegistry and ComponentRegistration to associate a supported component name with its validator and runtime factory.
  • TabularFileFormatRegistry capability checks for CSV and Parquet reading/writing.
  • ComponentCatalog and create_default_component_catalog() to compose shared registries, validators, factories, and the SQL engine factory.
  • PipelineBuilder to resolve all component types and preflight SQL environment-variable references before invoking component factories.
  • SQL engine caching, credential-aware error redaction, and explicit builder cleanup for configuration-built pipelines.
  • End-to-end tests for YAML/direct-Python equivalence, processor order, supported file/SQLite source-sink combinations, and rejection before external I/O or component construction.
  • User-facing documentation for schema version 1, supported properties and combinations, environment-variable references, error handling, architecture, and runnable examples.

Schema version 1 supports file sources/sinks with CSV and Parquet, SQL sources/sinks, local filesystem storage, and the select_columns, rename_columns, and filter_rows processors. It uses explicit registrations only; dynamic plugin loading, arbitrary imports, and eval are not supported. Missing or empty SQL environment variables fail during builder preflight before component factory construction and source/sink I/O.

The shared SQL engine factory is owned by the configuration-building lifecycle. Callers close the PipelineBuilder after a successfully built pipeline finishes execution. Direct Python SQL components retain their caller-owned engine contract.

Done when: A user can define a supported pipeline in YAML, load and validate it, build the same effective pipeline as direct Python composition, execute it, and diagnose configuration/preflight errors without leaking resolved connection URLs. Full regression and release checks pass.

docs.title: 0.7.0 — Command-line interface
docs.text:
Goal: Make the framework practical to run from a shell or automation script.

Initial commands:

  • etlrelay run pipeline.yaml
  • etlrelay validate pipeline.yaml
  • etlrelay version

Scope:

  • Define useful process exit codes.
  • Print actionable validation and execution errors.
  • Keep secrets and sensitive payloads out of terminal output.
  • Keep the CLI thin; pipeline construction and execution logic belong in the underlying library.
  • Test commands without requiring external databases or cloud resources for the unit suite.

Done when: A user can validate and run a supported YAML pipeline through the installed CLI.

docs.title: 0.8.0 — Security, errors, and operational readiness
docs.text:
Goal: Close cross-cutting gaps before the API is frozen.

Scope:

  • Review path containment and local storage behavior, including symlinks and output destinations.
  • Review SQL parameterization and identifier validation.
  • Validate configuration before side effects occur.
  • Establish a small, consistent exception/error-reporting policy without wrapping every error in a generic framework exception.
  • Add useful standard-library logging at component boundaries where needed.
  • Redact connection secrets, credentials, and sensitive values from errors/logging.
  • Document resource/stream ownership, overwrite behavior, empty-batch behavior, and failure propagation.
  • Add dependency and package checks to CI.
  • Verify the package can be installed and used from its built artifacts, not only from the repository checkout.

Done when: Security-relevant behavior is tested at the layer responsible for the risk, and failures are diagnosable without leaking secrets.

docs.title: 0.9.0 — Feature-complete beta and API review
docs.text:
Goal: Validate the intended v1.0 feature set and stop adding new features.

Scope:

  • Feature freeze.
  • Review public names, constructors, protocol signatures, configuration schema, CLI behavior, and documented exceptions.
  • Complete the pre-1.0.0 protocol naming cleanup: rename Reader and Writer to TabularReader and TabularWriter to make their Batch-oriented contracts explicit. Update concrete implementations, type annotations, public exports, tests, examples, and documentation consistently.
  • Keep KeyValueReader as a separate protocol for mapping-shaped documents. Confirm that configuration loading depends on this abstraction rather than the concrete YamlReader.
  • Decide whether KeyValueWriter has a concrete v1.0 use case before adding it; do not introduce it solely for symmetry.
  • Document the distinction between a mapping-shaped document and row records. Review possible tabular-to-records and records-to-tabular conversion contracts before the API freeze, but do not add a generic conversion framework without a demonstrated v1.0 use case.
  • Test full pipelines across supported combinations: local CSV, local Parquet, and SQL input/output.
  • Test empty inputs, empty batches, schema mismatches, malformed data, inaccessible resources, processor failures, sink failures, and stream cleanup.
  • Test a clean install on each supported Python version/platform combination the project claims to support.
  • Complete README, quick start, examples, API reference, configuration reference, security notes, contribution instructions, and release notes.
  • Document unsupported features and known limitations.

Done when: No required v1.0 feature remains unimplemented, release-blocking defects are resolved, and the project can maintain a clear public API contract. Reader/writer names clearly identify tabular contracts, the mapping-document contract is separate, and conversion scope is explicitly documented as either required or deferred.

docs.title: 1.0.0rc1 — Release candidate
docs.text: Cut a release candidate only after 0.9.0 has passed the feature-complete criteria. Use release candidates for final packaging validation, integration feedback, and defect correction—not new features. Publish another candidate if fixes materially affect the release, then proceed to 1.0.0 when the release criteria remain satisfied.

docs.title: 1.0.0 — Stable initial release
docs.text:
ETLRelay 1.0.0 is ready when a user can:

  1. Install the package using documented instructions.
  2. Define a supported pipeline in YAML.
  3. Read data from the local filesystem or a supported SQL source.
  4. Apply the documented set of built-in transformations.
  5. Write to a local file or supported SQL sink.
  6. Run the pipeline through the CLI.
  7. Diagnose failures using documented errors and logs.

The stable API, supported Python versions, supported input/output formats, configuration schema, CLI contract, and compatibility policy must be documented. Breaking changes to the public API after 1.0.0 should follow the project's published versioning policy.

docs.title: Potential post-1.0 expansions (not commitments)
docs.text:
The initial stable release intentionally focuses on config-driven execution of pipelines using local files and SQL. Additional integrations and capabilities may be considered after 1.0.0, based on use cases, maintenance cost, compatibility with the existing architecture, and available development effort.

Potential areas for future review include, but are not limited to:

  • Remote and distributed storage, including S3 and HDFS.
  • Additional database, data-warehouse, and analytical-platform integrations, potentially including Snowflake and Hive.
  • Excel and other file formats.
  • Generic API source/sink implementations.
  • Scheduling, retries, distributed processing, concurrency, and orchestration services.
  • Web UI, job queue, monitoring server, and data catalog/lineage systems.
  • Expanded custom-component loading or plugin mechanisms.
  • Larger processor libraries or a general-purpose expression language.
  • Tabular/record conversion utilities (for example, converting Batch data to a sequence of row mappings and back), if concrete use cases justify their contracts and maintenance cost.

These examples describe areas that may be evaluated, not features promised for a particular release. After v1.0.0, review candidate enhancements as a separate roadmap decision: identify concrete use cases, define acceptance criteria, estimate implementation and maintenance costs, and determine priority and sequencing. Do not assume that every listed integration will be implemented.

docs.title: Release hygiene
docs.text:
Before every public release:

  • Run the full test, lint, format, and type-check suites.
  • Build the wheel and source distribution.
  • Install and smoke-test the built package in a clean environment.
  • Review the changelog and release notes.
  • Ensure the version in package metadata matches the Git tag.
  • Test publication through TestPyPI when useful, then publish the actual release artifact.

The etlrelay distribution has already been published to PyPI; see the ETLRelay project page. Before each release, verify that package metadata, the built wheel and source distribution, the Git tag, and the release notes all identify the intended version. Revisit distribution-name availability only if the project proposes changing its published package name.

docs.text:
Version Status Milestone Release outcome 0.1.0 Released Experimental local CSV pipeline Initial local CSV pipeline published 0.1.x Released Stabilization Compatible fixes and documentation improvements 0.2.0 Released Batch contract and processors Basic useful transformations 0.3.0 Released Parquet CSV and Parquet through shared reader/writer interfaces 0.4.0 Released Storage contract stabilization Documented and tested local filesystem behavior; no remote-storage implementation 0.5.0 Released SQL source/sink Tested SQLite reads/writes and mixed file/SQL pipelines 0.6.0 Released YAML configuration Versioned schema validation, explicit component catalog, SQL preflight, and runtime pipeline construction 0.7.0 Planned CLI Validate and run pipelines from a shell 0.8.0 Planned Security and operational readiness Security review, errors/logging, installation and CI gates 0.9.0 Planned Feature-complete beta Feature freeze, reader/writer naming cleanup, and full API/representation-contract review 1.0.0rc1 Planned Release candidate Final validation and feedback 1.0.0 Planned Stable release Documented, usable, tested config-driven ETL product

Keep the principle constant: each release should deliver a coherent, tested increment, and the 1.0.0 milestone should mark API stability rather than feature abundance.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: ETLRelay 0.6.0 adds versioned YAML configuration, component validation, SQL environment-variable preflight, and a shared SQL engine factory for configuration-built pipelines. These features reduce ambiguity and prevent several classes of configuration error before data operations begin, but they do not form a full security boundary. ETLRelay remains pre-1.0 software; evaluate it in a controlled environment before using it for sensitive or production workloads.

docs.title: Local filesystem paths
docs.text:
PathValidator resolves candidate paths and verifies that resolved locations remain within the configured base directory. It checks path containment, not existence; the filesystem operation determines whether a read or write succeeds. Parent directories are not created automatically by the local filesystem implementation.

Path validation is not an operating-system sandbox and does not eliminate time-of-check/time-of-use races if another process can modify the filesystem concurrently. Run ETLRelay with only the filesystem permissions it needs and use a dedicated working directory where appropriate.

docs.title: YAML configuration safety
docs.text:
YamlReader uses a safe YAML loader. It rejects duplicate mapping keys, malformed documents, multiple documents where a single document is expected, non-mapping roots, and non-string root keys. It does not construct arbitrary Python objects from YAML tags.

ConfigValidator rejects unknown top-level fields, unknown component properties, unsupported component types, and unsupported schema versions. PipelineBuilder resolves explicit registrations; the v0.6.0 configuration format does not support arbitrary imports, eval, or unrestricted Python expression execution.

Configuration validation is not a guarantee that runtime inputs are trustworthy. SQL query text is still caller-authored SQL, and data-dependent column/schema constraints can fail during execution.

docs.title: SQL connection secrets
docs.text:
Use connection_url_env to name an environment variable containing a SQLAlchemy connection URL. Do not put credential-bearing connection URLs, passwords, API tokens, or other secrets directly in YAML files, examples, changelog entries, or version control.

During PipelineBuilder.build(), required connection-variable references are preflighted before ETL component factories run. Missing or empty values cause a PipelineBuildError before source/sink I/O begins. SqlEngineFactory avoids putting resolved connection URLs, credentials, or underlying driver exception text in its own error messages.

Environment variables provide indirection, not a secrets vault. Application deployment remains responsible for setting environment values securely, limiting who can inspect them, preventing them from leaking into logs or diagnostics, and rotating credentials when needed. Avoid logging environment dumps or complete connection URLs. Use a secrets manager or platform-native secret injection appropriate to the deployment when stronger lifecycle and access controls are required.

docs.title: SQL safety and limits
docs.text:
Use SQLAlchemy bound parameters for SQL values. Do not interpolate untrusted value data into SQL query strings. Bind parameters cannot represent table names, column names, operators, or sort direction; dynamic identifiers require a trusted allowlist and appropriate SQLAlchemy APIs.

SqlSource is not a SQL parser, query-policy engine, or authorization boundary. Use database credentials with the minimum required permissions. SqlSink appends to an existing table and does not implement a table-creation/migration or replace policy. SQLite is the reference integration-test backend; other SQLAlchemy dialects require suitable drivers and independent verification.

docs.title: Resource lifecycle
docs.text:
Direct Python SqlSource and SqlSink instances borrow the SQLAlchemy engine supplied by the caller; the application owns that engine and disposes it when it is no longer needed.

For YAML-built pipelines, create_default_component_catalog() creates or accepts a shared SqlEngineFactory, and the PipelineBuilder uses it for SQL components. The caller must invoke builder.close() after execution to release engines created by this shared factory and discard resolved URLs. Do not close a successful build's engine resources before the pipeline runs.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
ETLRelay does not provide a full filesystem sandbox, credentials vault, SQL authorization layer, external API security model, or remote-storage security model. Remote storage such as S3 and HDFS remains outside the planned v1.0.0 scope. Additional integrations require their own threat review and tests.

For reporting suspected vulnerabilities, follow the procedure in the repository's Security policy.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
ETLRelay 0.6.0 uses explicit registries to associate each supported configuration type with both its configuration validator and runtime factory. The validator and PipelineBuilder consume the same registrations, reducing the risk that a type is accepted during validation but unavailable during construction.

The registry is an internal composition mechanism, not a public dynamic-plugin system. The v0.6.0 default catalog defines a small fixed set of built-in components.

docs.title: Supported families
docs.text:
Family Registered names Registry Sources file, sql ComponentRegistry[Source] Sinks file, sql ComponentRegistry[Sink] Storage local ComponentRegistry[FileSystem] Processors select_columns, rename_columns, filter_rows ComponentRegistry[Processor] Tabular formats csv, parquet TabularFileFormatRegistry, with independent read/write capabilities Configuration document formats yaml KeyValueReader implementation; not part of the tabular format registry

Tabular formats are separate because a format can support reading, writing, or both. The format registry exposes capability queries without constructing readers/writers. YAML reads a mapping-shaped configuration document, not a stream of tabular Batch objects.

docs.title: Registration and dispatch
docs.text:
A ComponentRegistration[T] associates a ComponentConfigValidator with the factory used to build a component of type T. A ComponentRegistry[T] holds the explicit names and registrations for one family. Its lookup operation returns a registration or raises the registry's documented lookup error; it does not invoke the registration's factory.

The common ComponentConfigDispatcher checks mapping shape and the component type, then delegates validation through the matching registration. SourceConfigValidator, SinkConfigValidator, StorageConfigValidator, and ProcessorConfigValidator specialize this shared dispatch behavior with the appropriate registry and component-kind label. ProcessorSequenceConfigValidator validates the ordered list and delegates each element to the processor dispatcher with an indexed path.

Component-specific validators own their own property schema. The dispatcher does not contain file, sql, local, or processor-specific fields and never constructs runtime components.

docs.title: Default composition root
docs.text:
create_default_component_catalog() in etlrelay.default_component creates the shared registrations and services. It wires them in dependency order:

  1. Create the TabularFileFormatRegistry with CSV and Parquet readers and writers.
  2. Create the local storage registry and storage dispatcher.
  3. Create source and sink registrations that share the same storage and format registries where applicable.
  4. Create processor registrations pairing SelectColumns, RenameColumns, and FilterRows validators with their factories.
  5. Create source, sink, processor, and processor-sequence dispatchers.
  6. Create the root ConfigValidator and expose the shared objects through ComponentCatalog.

The caller may inject a SqlEngineFactory; otherwise the catalog creates one. The same SQL engine factory is injected into the built-in SQL source and sink factories and is exposed through the catalog for the builder's resource lifecycle.

Catalog creation instantiates registrations, validator objects, and factory objects. It does not call component factory build() methods, resolve SQL environment variables, create database engines, open data resources, or execute a pipeline.

docs.title: Pipeline construction
docs.text:
PipelineBuilder receives the source, sink, and processor registries from the same catalog. It resolves all registrations before SQL environment preflight or component construction. The order is deliberate: a configuration with an unknown component type or missing SQL URL must fail before any ETL component factory runs.

After all registrations and SQL references pass preflight, the builder constructs the source, processors in YAML order, and sink. It returns a Pipeline without executing it. If construction fails after SQL engines have been acquired during that attempt, the builder attempts to close the shared factory while preserving the original construction exception. On successful execution, the caller explicitly calls builder.close() to dispose the engines owned by the shared factory.

docs.title: Extension policy
docs.text:
Adding support for a component requires a runtime implementation, its component-specific configuration validator and factory, and one explicit registration in the default composition. It should not require changes to the generic registry, common dispatcher, unrelated validators, or ConfigValidator root rules, provided the root schema and supported component contract remain the same.

No automatic discovery, import-by-string, reflection-based construction, arbitrary user code execution, or mutable global service locator is provided in v0.6.0. New types must be intentionally added to the built-in configuration contract.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: ETLRelay 0.6.0 separates configuration-document parsing, schema validation, runtime component construction, and pipeline execution. The loader and validator stop at a validated mapping; the builder converts that mapping into runtime components only after resolving registrations and preflighting SQL environment references.

docs.title: End-to-end boundary
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[ConfigLoader.load path] --> B[FileSystem opens YAML file]
    B --> C[KeyValueReader.read stream]
    C --> D[YamlReader returns root mapping]
    D --> E[ConfigValidator.validate]
    E -->|valid mapping| F[PipelineBuilder.build]
    E -->|invalid schema| X[ConfigurationError]
    F --> G[Resolve all source, processor, and sink registrations]
    G --> H[SQL environment preflight]
    H -->|missing or empty reference| Y[PipelineBuildError]
    H --> I[Invoke component factories]
    I --> J[Return Pipeline]
    J --> K[Caller runs Pipeline.run]
    K --> L[Caller closes PipelineBuilder]

The configuration document itself has to be read. The no-side-effects guarantee concerns the configured ETL pipeline: schema validation does not open source/sink data files, connect to a database, create SQLAlchemy engines, invoke ETL component factories, or execute a pipeline. SQL URL environment variables are resolved during builder preflight; engines are created lazily when SQL component factories request them after successful preflight.

docs.title: KeyValueReader and YamlReader
docs.text:
KeyValueReader is a format-independent protocol for reading one mapping-shaped document from a binary stream. It is distinct from the tabular Reader protocol, which produces an iterable of ETLRelay Batch objects.

YamlReader lives in etlrelay.readers.yaml. It uses a safe PyYAML loader, rejects duplicate mapping keys (including duplicates after merge-key flattening), requires one document whose root is a mapping, and requires string keys at the root. It does not know ETLRelay's allowed configuration fields and does not perform application-schema validation. YamlReader leaves the supplied stream lifecycle to its caller.

docs.title: ConfigLoader
docs.text:
ConfigLoader receives a FileSystem, a KeyValueReader, and a ConfigValidator. load(path) opens the configuration resource through the injected filesystem, passes the stream to the reader within a context manager, validates the parsed object, and returns the mapping on success. It does not select a reader by file extension, construct components, resolve SQL variables, create engines, build a pipeline, or execute it.

ConfigLoader does not broadly translate exceptions. YAML parsing errors and filesystem errors propagate in their own exception types; schema validation failures are reported by ConfigurationError.

docs.title: ConfigValidator
docs.text:
ConfigValidator checks root-level properties and schema version 1, then delegates to the source, processor-sequence, and sink validators. Root values must be mappings with string keys. The root keys must be exactly version, source, processors, and sink, all required. The integer version check explicitly rejects YAML Boolean true.

Leaf and family validators return path-qualified error strings. ConfigValidator.validate() raises ConfigurationError when the root checks or any delegated validation produces errors; on success it returns None. The parsed mapping is returned by ConfigLoader.load(), not by the validator.

docs.title: PipelineBuilder
docs.text:
PipelineBuilder consumes validated configuration. It first resolves all source, sink, and processor registrations; then it collects SQL environment-variable references from configured SQL sources/sinks and performs preflight. It invokes component factories only after those steps succeed. Processors are constructed in YAML order.

The builder returns a Pipeline but does not execute it. With the default catalog, SQL source and sink factories share the catalog's SqlEngineFactory. Once the pipeline finishes, the caller calls builder.close() to dispose factory-owned engines and discard resolved URLs. Direct Python SqlSource/SqlSink usage retains the direct API's caller-owned engine lifecycle.

If component construction fails after SQL engines have been created in that build attempt, the builder attempts cleanup and preserves the original construction exception. A successful build must not close SQL resources before pipeline execution.

docs.title: Why parsing and validation are separate
docs.text:
A mapping document format reader knows YAML syntax, duplicate keys, document count, and root shape. The validator knows the ETLRelay schema—allowed component types, property names, property types, required fields, and schema version. Keeping these responsibilities separate permits a future mapping reader (such as JSON) without making it responsible for ETLRelay component names.

A future document format does not need to be part of the tabular TabularFileFormatRegistry. That registry is specifically about the ability to read and/or write tabular batches in CSV, Parquet, or another future tabular format.

docs.title: Error boundaries
docs.text: Boundary Examples Error behavior YAML parsing / shape Malformed YAML, duplicate mapping keys, multiple documents PyYAML error or ValueError from YamlReader for root-shape violations. Root and component schema Unsupported version, missing/unknown fields, invalid field types ConfigurationError raised by ConfigValidator. Build and preflight Unsupported/unregistered types, missing or empty SQL environment variables PipelineBuildError. Runtime execution File, query, schema, processor, or sink failures Underlying runtime exceptions propagate unless a component contract explicitly translates them.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The implementation intentionally has no CLI, arbitrary dynamic imports, expression evaluation, automatic plugin discovery, configuration inheritance, templating, or JSON reader. The v0.6.0 public workflow is the YAML loader/validator, the shared default component catalog, and PipelineBuilder, with the CLI remaining a roadmap item.

See YAML Configuration, Configuration Validation Architecture, and Component Registry Architecture.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
ETLRelay 0.6.0 validates a versioned mapping-shaped configuration before runtime components are constructed. Validation uses explicit component registrations and component-specific validators; it does not use dynamic discovery, reflection, arbitrary imports, or Python expression evaluation.

The version-1 schema is specified in the YAML Configuration reference. This page documents how that contract is validated and how validation differs from construction and execution.

docs.title: Validation layers
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Mapping from KeyValueReader] --> B[ConfigValidator]
    B --> C[Root fields and schema version]
    C --> D[SourceConfigValidator]
    C --> E[ProcessorSequenceConfigValidator]
    C --> F[SinkConfigValidator]
    D --> G[ComponentConfigDispatcher]
    F --> H[ComponentConfigDispatcher]
    E --> I[Validate list and each indexed processor]
    G --> J[Registered source validator]
    H --> K[Registered sink validator]
    I --> L[ProcessorConfigValidator]
    J --> M[Aggregate error strings]
    K --> M
    L --> M
    C --> M
    M --> N{Any errors?}
    N -->|yes| O[ConfigurationError]
    N -->|no| P[Validation succeeds]

docs.title: Root schema validator
docs.text:
ConfigValidator accepts an object so it can defensively validate calls made outside the usual loader. It requires a mapping with string keys, rejects unknown top-level fields, requires version, source, processors, and sink, and requires the actual integer 1 for version—a Boolean is not accepted even though bool is an int subclass in Python.

When the root object cannot safely be interpreted as a string-keyed mapping, the validator raises ConfigurationError before delegating to section validators. Otherwise it checks root fields and delegates each present section to the injected source, processor-sequence, and sink validators. Errors are aggregated into one ConfigurationError rather than raising for each ordinary invalid property.

docs.title: Validator contract
docs.text:
ComponentConfigValidator is a Protocol exposing validate(config: object, path: str) -> list[str]. Concrete component validators return path-qualified error strings. An empty list indicates that no validation errors were found; a normal schema failure is not represented by an exception at the leaf-validator level.

This shared protocol applies to source/sink/storage dispatch and individual processors. The processor-sequence validator uses the same protocol to validate each list element.

docs.title: Dispatch and leaf validators
docs.text:
ComponentConfigDispatcher is the common dispatcher used by SourceConfigValidator, SinkConfigValidator, StorageConfigValidator, and ProcessorConfigValidator. It validates that the component configuration is a mapping with string keys, checks that type is a non-empty string, looks up the registration in its registry, and delegates to the registered validator. Invalid or unregistered types return path-specific validation messages. Validation does not invoke component factories.

Leaf validators own their own property rules:

  • File source: required path, format, and nested storage; the format registry must support reading.
  • File sink: required path, format, and nested storage; the format registry must support writing.
  • SQL source: connection-variable name and query are non-empty strings; optional parameters are a mapping of string keys to scalar strings, numbers, Booleans, or None.
  • SQL sink: connection-variable name and table name are required non-empty strings; optional schema is a non-empty string.
  • Local storage: type: local; optional base_path must be a non-empty string when present.
  • select_columns: required list of unique strings.
  • rename_columns: required mapping with string keys and values; data-dependent source/final-name constraints remain at processing time.
  • filter_rows: required non-empty column name, one of six supported comparison operators, and a string/integer/float/Boolean value (no null).

File source/sink validators share the storage validator and tabular file-format registry. They do not open data files. Format validation checks registry capabilities without constructing readers or writers.

docs.title: Processor sequence validation
docs.text: ProcessorSequenceConfigValidator requires a list and accepts an empty list. It visits each element in order and delegates to the processor dispatcher using paths such as processors[0] and processors[1]. Errors from an invalid element do not stop later elements from being validated. A missing root processors property is a root-level error; it is not equivalent to an empty list.

docs.title: Schema validation versus runtime validation
docs.text:
Configuration validation can check that a column list contains unique strings, but it cannot establish whether the source data contains those column names. It can check that a SQL query string and scalar parameters have supported types, but it does not execute the query. It can check a table-name string, but it does not connect to a database or verify that the destination table exists. Similarly, local path syntax/containment validation does not prove that the data file exists or is accessible.

Environment-variable names are part of the configuration and can be checked for shape during schema validation. Whether a connection-variable name resolves to a non-empty value is checked by PipelineBuilder's SQL preflight, before component factory construction and source/sink I/O.

docs.title: Representative errors
docs.text:
Invalid configuration Example diagnostic Unsupported version version must be the integer 1. Unknown field source.fomrat is not a supported field. Missing discriminator source.type is required. Unsupported format sink.format 'xlsx' is not supported for writing. Invalid processor operator processors[0].operator must be one of '==', '!=', '<', '<=', '>', '>='.

Component validators aggregate ordinary validation errors as lists. ConfigValidator raises ConfigurationError with collected errors. Exact exception rendering depends on the exception's implemented string representation; the messages above illustrate the underlying validation diagnostics.

docs.title: Test responsibilities
docs.text:
• Leaf-validator unit tests use plain values and do not open files or connect to databases.
  • Dispatcher tests use fake/mocked registrations and assert the correct validator receives the original configuration and exact path.
  • Processor-sequence tests cover empty lists, non-lists, ordered indexed paths, and aggregation across multiple invalid entries.
  • Root-validator tests cover string-keyed mappings, required/unknown fields, strict integer version handling, delegation order, and aggregated errors.
  • Integration/functional tests exercise the actual default catalog and YAML loader; pipeline-builder tests separately verify preflight and no component construction on early failure.

See Configuration Loading Architecture and Component Registry Architecture.
